title: Extending Collatz k-Cycle Exclusion via Case Analysis
description: Addresses OQ-01 of the Collatz cycle non-existence problem: can parity case analysis be extended to rule out k-cycles for small k ≥ 4? Proves the j=1 algebraic uniqueness theorem (3n+1 = 2^M·n forces n=1, M=2), extends the halving constraint bounds to j=5..8 odd steps, and establishes minimum cycle lengths. Axiomatizes the Eliahou (1993) bound: any non-trivial cycle has period > 17 billion.

meta.author: Research formalization 2026
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: eliahou_cycle_bound — Eliahou (1993) proved any non-trivial Collatz cycle has period > 17 billion (Discrete Math 118:45–56). Fully machine-verified results: j=1 uniqueness theorem, halving bounds j=5..8, minimum cycle lengths, case complexity lower bound.

overview.historicalContext: The Collatz conjecture is equivalent to the non-existence of cycles other than {1,4,2}. Lagarias (1985) systematized the algebraic approach via the 2^M > 3^j constraint, and Eliahou (1993) pushed this to a lower bound of 17 billion on any non-trivial cycle's length. The parity case analysis approach (ruling out fixed points and 2-cycles directly) raises the natural question: how far can it go? This file shows it works cleanly for the j=1 (algebraic uniqueness) case and can verify specific small k via interval_cases, but the exponential growth of parity patterns (2^k) makes it infeasible for large k without the algebraic machinery.
overview.problemStatement: **OQ-01**: Can parity case analysis be extended to rule out Collatz k-cycles for specific small k ≥ 4? What are the minimum lengths for cycles with j = 5..8 odd steps?
overview.text: Extends the CollatzCycles.lean analysis with the j=1 uniqueness theorem and halving bounds for j=5..8, establishing minimum cycle lengths and quantifying the exponential case explosion that limits direct case analysis.
overview.proofStrategy: The j=1 uniqueness theorem is proved algebraically: 3n+1 = 2^M·n rearranges to n·(2^M-3)=1, forcing n|1 and n=1 (with M=2). For j≥2 in small cycles, the 2^(k-j) > 3^j constraint is verified by norm_num. Extended halving bounds for j=5..8 use interval_cases with norm_num. The Eliahou bound is axiomatized.
keyInsights: The j=1 uniqueness theorem provides a purely algebraic proof that the only 1-odd-step Collatz cycle is {1,4,2}.
For a period-4 cycle: j=1 requires (3n+1)/8=n → 5n=1 (impossible); j=2,3,4 all violate 2^(4-j) > 3^j.
Halving bounds grow as ⌈j·log₂3⌉ ≈ 1.585·j, so minimum cycle lengths grow roughly as 2.585·j.
The number of parity patterns for a k-cycle is 2^k — ruling out all patterns requires exponentially more work.
Eliahou (1993) used algebraic sum bounds (not case analysis) to prove the 17-billion lower bound in one argument.

sections.title: The j=1 Cycle Uniqueness Theorem
sections.summary: Proves that 3n+1 = 2^M·n has the unique ℕ solution n=1, M=2. The proof: n·(2^M-3)=1 forces n|1 so n=1, then M=2. Corollary: no 1-odd-step cycle has period ≥ 4.

sections.title: Algebraic Constraints for Period-4 Cycles
sections.summary: Shows all parity distributions for 4-cycles fail: j=2,3,4 violate 2^(4-j)>3^j; j=1 gives (3n+1)/8=n → 5n=1, impossible.
sections.mathContext: For j=2: $4 > 9$ false; j=3: $2 > 27$ false; j=4: $1 > 81$ false; j=1: $(3n+1)/8 = n \Rightarrow 5n = 1$, impossible.

sections.title: Extended Halving Constraints (j=5..8)
sections.summary: Proves min halvings for j=5 (M≥8), j=6 (M≥10), j=7 (M≥12), j=8 (M≥13) via interval_cases with norm_num.

sections.title: Minimum Cycle Lengths (j=5..8)
sections.summary: Derives min cycle lengths: j=5→≥13, j=6→≥16, j=7→≥19, j=8→≥21.
sections.mathContext: Cycle length $= j + M \geq j + \lceil j \log_2 3 \rceil \approx 2.585j$.

sections.title: Case Analysis Complexity
sections.summary: Proves 2^k parity patterns for k-cycles grow exponentially. Computing examples: k=4→16, k=10→1024, k=20→1M patterns.
sections.mathContext: Parity patterns for a $k$-cycle: $2^k$ (each of $k$ orbit elements is odd or even).

sections.title: Eliahou Bound and OQ-01 Resolution
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Eliahou (1993): non-trivial cycles have period > 17 billion. Proves OQ-01 corollary: all cycles of period ≤ 17 billion reduce to {1,4,2}.
sections.mathContext: Eliahou (1993): any non-trivial Collatz cycle has period $> 1.7 \times 10^{10}$.

conclusion.summary: Case analysis can rule out k-cycles for small k via explicit algebraic constraints, but requires exponentially growing work (2^k parity patterns). The j=1 uniqueness theorem provides a clean algebraic proof that the only 1-odd-step cycle is {1,4,2}. Extended halving bounds cover j=5..8. Eliahou's deeper algebraic methods give the definitive 17-billion lower bound.
conclusion.implications: The OQ-01 question is answered: case analysis works for fixed small k but cannot scale to an unrestricted answer. The Eliahou bound axiom, once formalized from Eliahou's original paper, would eliminate the axiom and make this entry fully verified.
openQuestions: Can Eliahou's 1993 proof be formalized in Lean using Mathlib's arithmetic tools?
Can Tao's 2019 almost-all result be formalized using Mathlib measure theory?
What is the exact minimum cycle length for j=9..12 odd steps?
